selected_problem: Fresh-main V14 effect lifecycle permits stale first attempt, stale same-key retry and unbound internal caller progression into COMMITTING because effect reservation/attempt/provider-precommit are not immutably bound to the admitted singleton execution generation.
hypothesis: A ClayCode-semantic execution-generation fence, atomically persisted with EffectReservation and rechecked at first attempt, retry and provider-precommit, prevents stale or successor holders from recovering external-effect authority while preserving late outcome evidence for reconciliation.
strongest_counterhypothesis: V15 singleton presence plus the Linux physical execution lock are already sufficient; adding a durable generation fence only duplicates state, increases migration/recovery complexity and can discard useful provider evidence after holder turnover.

external_evidence.source: AWS Builders Library: Making retries safe with idempotent APIs
external_evidence.use: Timeouts can leave side effects uncertain; retries need idempotency identity and uncertain outcomes may require reconciliation.
A lock alone does not prevent delayed stale holders from acting; fencing tokens must be checked by the protected resource.

fresh_state_findings: Current repo program is unified FRANK_V0_1; H1/H2/H3 are not active products/stages.
A previously tested strict V16.1 candidate existed but its branch was stale relative to main.

The old candidate was developed against byte-identical baseline blobs for frank_effects.clay and effect_lifecycle_runtime.py, enabling mechanism-level porting without assuming stale branch ancestry is current truth.

A stale-port regression was caught: the imported apply_current_schema.py omitted current V16 execution continuity. The branch was corrected so V16 remains immediately before V16.1; the resulting PR diff now only adds V16.1 to the current migration chain.
The ClayCode compatibility facade still had an unfenced two-argument reserve call; it was corrected to carry EffectExecutionFence.
The WP04 effect-contract probe still described the old unfenced reserve/execute signatures; it was corrected to the fenced contract.
A final runtime provider_commit_fence was added so generation validity is rechecked immediately before trusted provider emission, not only at transition into COMMITTING.
The SQL effect_id->execution-generation binding was strengthened with fail-closed UPDATE and DELETE immutability triggers.

A sealed production Python carrier was added ahead of the trusted low-level lifecycle primitive. It can be minted only from a live FrankExecutionLease or the canonical IngressExecutionLease that contains one; raw epoch/session/client field bundles are rejected at this production surface.

Current main advanced twice during the run; both deltas were compared before integration and were disjoint from the effect-fence implementation. Main was merged into the candidate branch rather than overwriting newer shared work.

clay_semantics: begin_effect_attempt binds reservation generation to current execution
execute rechecks exact execution generation immediately before runtime_effect
persistence: atomic reservation + optional confirmation consumption + execution-generation fence
runtime: begin_attempt and retry require stored fence == presented generation == current V15 holder
provider_commit_fence repeats the same equality at the last pre-provider boundary
outcome/reconciliation admission intentionally does not require the old holder to remain current
production_boundary: FencedEffectLifecycleRuntime accepts the capability instead of raw generation fields
capability derives from FrankExecutionLease / canonical IngressExecutionLease
closing the underlying execution lease revokes the process-local capability

exactly_one_out_of_box_experiment.name: CAPABILITY_TIME_CAPSULE
exactly_one_out_of_box_experiment.question: Can a serialized/already-COMMITTING effect capability from generation A regain provider or retry authority after generation B becomes current?
exactly_one_out_of_box_experiment.interpretation: The selected equality relation removes modeled stale provider/retry authority across the enumerated turnover space. This is synthetic only and cannot substitute for current-source Ubuntu execution evidence.

v17_fusion.finding: Execution-generation fencing and V17/V17.1 causal completion address adjacent but distinct authority boundaries: who may perform/retry the external effect versus which verified outcome may causally reach re-entry/DONE.
v17_fusion.counterevidence_preserved: V17 relational cross-splice discriminator demonstrated that a richer completion schema could accept unrelated causal-credit/snapshot support. Therefore neither V17 completion nor this fence is treated as whole-effect-authority completion.
